sections.h2: What routes exist for selling a Perrysburg house quickly?
sections.html:
An owner here can hire a broker, market the property alone, or sell to a cash buyer who absorbs the repair bill. Perrysburg lies in Wood County, which means deeds, tax bills and building permits involve county offices as well as city hall. Knowing who handles each task keeps a sale from stalling at the last step.

  • A broker listing fits a house that can pass a lender's appraisal and survive weeks of showings.
  • Selling alone works when a closing agent or a lawyer drafts the deed and the settlement sheet.
  • A cash sale fits estate houses, occupied rentals and homes with a long repair list.

sections.h2: Where does Perrysburg come from, and what did that leave behind?
sections.html:
Perrysburg is a Wood County city on the south bank of the Maumee River, about 12 miles southwest of Toledo. Federal surveyors platted it in the summer of 1816, and the name honors Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry. Fort Meigs, begun in February 1813 on a bluff above the water, is the largest wooden walled fortification in North America, and two critical battles with the British took place there during the War of 1812.

The settlement grew on shipbuilding and river trade. It was the county seat from 1822 to 1868 and gained a railroad in 1859. The seat later moved to Bowling Green, where courthouse construction began in November 1893. Along the way, a cholera epidemic in 1854 killed more than 100 people, and the early settlers of Orleans had to relocate to higher ground after floods.

The area lies near the center of the Twelve Mile Square Reservation, land the Odawa ceded to the United States in 1795, and the 1817 Treaty of Fort Meigs ended their claim to this stretch of the river. The first plat spanned 1.786 square miles. Today the city measures 11.51 square miles by the 2010 count, so most houses stand on land added long after that plat.

sections.h2: What do Perrysburg incomes and home values look like?
sections.html:
The median Perrysburg owner-occupied home is valued at $329,700, and the median household earns $111,643. Just under two thirds of homes are lived in by their owners, so a sizeable share of the housing is rented.

The city counted 20,623 residents in 2010, so it has added roughly 4,800 in fifteen years. Retail sales in 2022 came to $28,217 per person, and Levis Commons is the best-known retail center in town.

sections.h2: Which employers, schools and shopping areas support the Perrysburg market?
sections.html:
Companies headquartered in the city include Owens-Illinois, a global glass container maker, Burkett Restaurant Equipment and Universal Tube and Rollform Equipment. Levis Commons is the best-known place to shop and eat.

Perrysburg Schools operate a preschool, four elementary schools, an intermediate school, a junior high and Perrysburg High School. Saint Rose School and The Islamic School of Greater Toledo also serve families, and the Way Public Library covers the Perrysburg area.

Education levels run high locally. Among residents 25 and older, 57.6% hold at least a bachelor's degree, and the commute averages 18.9 minutes.

sections.h2: Who approves permits for a Perrysburg house: the city or Wood County?
sections.html:
Both. The City of Perrysburg grants zoning permits, and it contracts with Wood County Building Inspection for building permits, with the zoning permit coming first. The Planning and Zoning Division enforces codified ordinance Chapters 1210 through 1460 and also handles code enforcement, Board of Zoning Appeals applications and Historic Landmarks Commission cases.

The division's published answers help a seller who is closing out old projects:

  • Any change in a fence's height, style or location needs a permit.
  • Each new shed needs one, including a freestanding unit not fixed to the ground, and it must sit at least 5 feet off the lot line and 10 feet from the house.
  • Trailers and recreational vehicles may stay in a front or side yard between April 1 and October 31, on a hard surface at least 5 feet from any lot line.
  • City staff do not survey lots, so use a certified surveyor to find boundaries.

Zoning questions go to the office at 201 W Indiana Avenue, phone 419-872-8060. Building permit questions go to Wood County Building Inspection at 419-354-9190 on weekdays between 7:30 and 3:30, or toll free at 866-860-4140.

Landlords carry an extra obligation. Rental owners in Perrysburg must file a net profit income tax return on rental income and report tenants who move in or out.

sections.h2: How do Wood County deed filing and tax bills work for a Perrysburg seller?
sections.html:
After closing, the deed visits the Wood County Auditor before it reaches the recorder. Under Ohio Revised Code 322.02, any county transfer tax is paid by the grantor to the auditor when the deed is delivered, ahead of recording, and section 319.202 requires the buyer to submit a statement of value. The auditor answers at 419-354-9150 or 866-860-4140.

The Wood County Treasurer collects real estate tax in two installments, due in February and July. About eighty taxing districts exist in the county, each with its own rate, so a Perrysburg bill reflects the levies at that address. Payments go by mail to the treasurer at 1 Courthouse Square in Bowling Green or to participating banks, several with Perrysburg branches, until close of business on the due date, and mailed payments must be postmarked by then. and a 5 percent penalty applies for the first 10 days after it, rising to 10 percent after that, as Ohio Revised Code 323.13 sets out.

Ohio's property disclosure statute, section 5302.30, tells you to hand buyers the state form promptly. It asks about the water supply, the sewer system, the roof and foundation, and defects you know of. Fiduciary transfers from an estate and inherited houses that you did not occupy in the past year are exempt.

sections.h2: When does a cash purchase suit a Perrysburg owner?
sections.html:
Cash suits cases where timing or condition outweighs the final dollar: an inherited Perrysburg house nobody will renovate, a tenant-occupied rental, or a move for work on a short schedule. The buyer purchases the house with its flaws, so you skip contractors, showings and appraisal waits.

Ask for the offer in writing and set it beside a realistic listing result after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Find out who pays the transfer charges, which date closes the sale, and what happens if the buyer finds a defect. Declining an offer does not stop you from listing.

faqs.q: Who issues a building permit for a Perrysburg house?
faqs.a: Wood County Building Inspection, after the City of Perrysburg has issued a zoning permit. The zoning permit must be obtained before the building permit is released.

faqs.q: Does swapping out a fence in Perrysburg need a permit?
faqs.a: A permit is required any time a fence changes in height, style or location. For a replacement identical in height, style and position, confirm with Planning and Zoning at 419-872-8060 before starting.

faqs.q: When do Wood County tax bills come due?
faqs.a: In February and July each year. Pay late and a 5 percent penalty applies during the first 10 days, then 10 percent.

faqs.q: Do Perrysburg landlords owe the city income tax on rent?
faqs.a: Yes. The city asks owners of rental property to file a net profit income tax return for rental income and to report tenants who occupy or leave their units.

faqs.q: Which disclosures apply when I sell a Perrysburg home?
faqs.a: The state form under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 applies, covering the water supply, sewer system, structure, hazardous materials and known defects, delivered to buyers promptly.
